root_cause.result: Connection ownership is appropriate, but separate current-thread runtimes add a mandatory remote wake boundary. Removing the named h2 lock stage does not make this topology faster.
root_cause.native_all_thread: Immediate-prior to candidate named h2 mutex-wait leaves: 85 to 0; mutex-drop leaves: 20 to 0. These counts include waiting, are not CPU percentages and do not prove zero h2 contention.
root_cause.observed_chain: run_worker -> publish_batch -> BatchTransportState.submit/flush/send_group -> Tokio wake_by_val -> I/O driver Handle.unpark -> kevent. One exact captured chain accounts for 221ms sampled CPU; not a complete category total.
root_cause.source_cause: Tokio 1.53.0 current_thread::Handle.schedule pushes externally scheduled tasks into its remote queue and unconditionally unparks the driver. Driver.unpark calls mio 1.2.2 Waker; macOS kqueue wake issues kevent. Shared-runtime local scheduling can avoid that cross-runtime syscall.
root_cause.go_comparison: grpc-go v1.79.3 http2_client.go starts connection-owned reader and loopy-writer goroutines. Go does not dedicate a separate runtime or pinned OS thread to each connection. Connection ownership alone does not justify this Rust runtime split.
root_cause.limits: Controlled measurements isolate the topology regression versus immediate prior. Profiles and source establish an added wake stage, not a complete numerical attribution of the 6.96 percent SQL CPU increase or the entire faster-control gap.

next_action: Keep connection lifecycle ownership while removing unnecessary cross-runtime wake handoffs. Compare pinned Go and both Rust topologies before the next connected edit. Retest once per coherent change and accept only matched SQL with higher throughput/lower latency; do not infer a win from fewer named locks.
